Simulate data from a bmm model

Source: R/simulate-data.R
simulate_data.Rd

simulate_data() draws data from a model given the values of its parameters and a design, in the layout bmm() expects for that model: the design's columns with the response columns added under the names the model was specified with. The result can be passed to bmm() as it is, which is what a parameter recovery study needs.

Usage

simulate_data(model, pars, design = NULL, scale = c("link", "native"), ...)

# Default S3 method
simulate_data(model, pars, design = NULL, scale = c("link", "native"), ...)

Arguments

model

A bmmodel object, such as mixture2p(resp_error = "y").

pars

A named list of parameter values, named as parameter_info() lists the model's parameters, or a data frame of them with one row or one row per row of design, such as the attribute simulate_pars of an earlier result. Each value is a single number or a vector with one element per row of design, element i going to row i. Parameters the model fixes may be left out, and then take their fixed value; a value given for one of them replaces it. Of alternative parameters, such as criterion and bias of sdt_yn(), give one.

design

A data frame with one row per observation of the model's data: one trial for trial-level models, one cell for the models of response counts. It holds the columns the model reads (see the section Design) and any others, such as condition labels or a subject identifier, which are returned unchanged. NULL for the models that read no column, and then n_trials in ... gives the number of observations.

scale

The scale of the values in pars. "link" (the default) is the scale bmm() estimates the parameters on and summary() reports, for example kappa on the log scale. "native" is the scale after the inverse of the model's link, the scale of native_parameters(): kappa as a precision, thetat of mixture2p() as the probability of recall. The weights of a softmax group, such as thetat and thetant of mixture3p(), are given as the probabilities themselves. They are the weights of a display with non-targets; where the set size is 1, the non-target weight goes to the target and to guessing in proportion, as in the fit, so thetat = 0.6 with thetant = 0.2 gives a probability of recall of 0.75 there.

...

n_trials, the number of observations when design is NULL; formula, the bmmformula() with the activation functions, for the custom version of m3(), whose parameters exist only in that formula.

Value

A data frame: design with the response columns added. It carries the attribute simulate_pars, a data frame with the value of every parameter (fixed ones included) for every row on the link scale, the values a recovery study compares the estimates with, and simulate_call, the model's class and the scale. For ezdm(), rows whose simulated mean response time is not positive are dropped with a warning, because bmm() rejects them; their row numbers are in the attribute dropped_rows. A mean response time below the non-decision time is a valid draw and is kept.

Details

The values are converted from the link scale with the inverse of each parameter's link, by the code native_parameters() uses, so that a softmax group and the set-size gate of the non-target weights of mixture3p() (no non-target weight where no non-target was shown) are applied as in the fit. Some parameters are defined on a transformed scale behind an identity link, such as sdratio of sdt_rating(), the log of the ratio of the standard deviations. For those, "native" is the value itself; the transformation to the argument of the random number generator (here exp(sdratio)) is applied on both scales.

The data are drawn with the model's r*() function, such as rmixture2p() or rsdt_rating(). They are not independent of the model's density functions: a recovery study that has to rule out an error shared by the two needs a generator written separately.

Design

The columns each model reads from design, under the names the model was specified with:

ModelColumns
sdm(), ddm(), cswald()none
mixture2p()set_size (if it names a column) for the versions "slot" and "slot_averaging"; none for "simple"
mixture3p()set_size (if it names a column), nt_features, of which a row's first set_size - 1 are read
imm()as mixture3p(), plus nt_distances for the versions "full" and "bsc"
m3()n_trials, the number of trials of each row; num_options when it names columns; for the custom version, the columns its activation functions read besides the parameters, as numbers (code a factor as 0/1 indicators)
mpt()n_trials; tree_id and covariates when the model has them
ezdm()n_trials
sdt_yn()stimulus, n_trials
sdt_mafc()n_trials; m when it names a column
sdt_ranking()n_trials; m when it names a column
sdt_rating(), sdt_cdp()stimulus, n_trials
psychometric_function()intensity; n_trials when it names a column (else each row is one 0/1 trial); guess and lapse when they name columns

The simplex groups of mpt() are given as probabilities that sum to 1 on both scales.

Examples

# circular responses: two-parameter mixture model, 100 trials
data <- bmm::simulate_data(mixture2p(resp_error = "y"),
  pars = list(kappa = log(8), thetat = 0.5), n_trials = 100
)
head(data)
#>             y
#> 1  0.79624383
#> 2  0.01005821
#> 3 -0.24949631
#> 4 -0.48835639
#> 5 -2.38609265
#> 6 -0.65857191
attr(data, "simulate_pars")[1, ]
#>   mu    kappa thetat
#> 1  0 2.079442    0.5

# the same on the native scale: kappa as a precision, thetat as P(memory)
data <- bmm::simulate_data(mixture2p(resp_error = "y"),
  pars = list(kappa = 8, thetat = 0.62), scale = "native", n_trials = 100
)

# response times and decisions: one value of the drift rate per trial
design <- data.frame(cond = rep(c("easy", "hard"), each = 50))
data <- bmm::simulate_data(ddm(rt = "rt", response = "response"),
  pars = list(drift = ifelse(design$cond == "easy", 2, 0.5), bound = 0, ndt = -1.5),
  design = design
)
head(data)
#>   cond        rt response
#> 1 easy 0.3266617        1
#> 2 easy 0.4780491        1
#> 3 easy 0.3817034        1
#> 4 easy 0.5858332        1
#> 5 easy 0.3244656        1
#> 6 easy 0.3514862        1

# counts: yes/no recognition, 50 trials per stimulus type
design <- data.frame(stimulus = c(0, 1), n_trials = 50)
bmm::simulate_data(sdt_yn(response = "n_old", stimulus = "stimulus", n_trials = "n_trials"),
  pars = list(d = 1.5, criterion = 0.5), design = design
)
#>   stimulus n_trials n_old
#> 1        0       50    18
#> 2        1       50    42

# categorical responses: memory measurement model, 100 trials per row
model <- m3(
  resp_cats = c("corr", "other", "npl"), num_options = c(1, 4, 5),
  choice_rule = "softmax", version = "ss"
)
bmm::simulate_data(model, pars = list(c = 2, a = 0.5), design = data.frame(n_trials = c(100, 100)))
#>   n_trials corr other npl
#> 1      100   57    23  20
#> 2      100   43    31  26
